items.text: A sub's contract is 40,000 dollars and it has received 25,000 dollars in payments. What is the maximum construction lien it can claim?
B. 15,000 dollars - contract price less payments received — MCL 570.1107(1) caps a lien at the claimant's contract price less payments received - here 15,000 dollars.
Several subs record liens on a homeowner's project. What is the ceiling on the SUM of all the liens?

D. The amount the owner agreed to pay the contractor, less payments made through sworn statements or lien waivers — MCL 570.1107(6) limits the sum of all liens to what the owner agreed to pay the contractor, less payments made pursuant to sworn statement or lien waiver - the residential no-double-payment protection.
On a COMMERCIAL project, how is the Notice of Commencement handled?

A. The owner records it with the register of deeds before physical improvement begins — MCL 570.1108 requires the commercial owner to record the Notice of Commencement with the register of deeds before physical improvement begins; the on-request, not-recorded procedure is the residential rule under section 1108a.
Which party is NOT required to serve a Notice of Furnishing?

C. The general contractor in direct contract with the owner — MCL 570.1109(1) expressly excuses a contractor in privity with the owner from the Notice of Furnishing requirement; subs, suppliers, and laborers must serve one.
On whom must a subcontractor serve its Notice of Furnishing?

D. The designee and the general contractor named in the Notice of Commencement, personally or by certified mail — MCL 570.1109(1) requires service personally or by certified mail on the designee and the general contractor named in the Notice of Commencement (owner or lessee if no designee); certified-mail service is complete on mailing.
A laborer's fringe benefits for March go unpaid. By when must the Notice of Furnishing for those fringes be served?

B. By the fifth day of the second month after the month they were due but unpaid — MCL 570.1109(3) sets the laborer fringe-benefit notice deadline at the 5th day of the second month after the month the benefits were due but unpaid; the 30-day rule covers unpaid wages.
A drywall sub serves its Notice of Furnishing 45 days after first furnishing - 25 days late. What is the effect on its lien?

C. Work after the notice is protected, and earlier work too, except amounts the owner already paid the contractor under a sworn statement or lien waiver — Under MCL 570.1109(5)-(6) a late notice does not kill the lien: post-notice work is fully protected and pre-notice work is protected except to the extent the owner already paid for it via sworn statement or lien waiver.
A laborer misses the 30-day deadline for the Notice of Furnishing on unpaid wages. What is the effect on the wage lien?

A. The wage lien is defeated outright — MCL 570.1109(7) defeats a laborer wage lien outright when the laborer notice is missed - unlike the sub and supplier rule, where a late notice still gives partial protection.
When must a contractor provide the owner with a sworn statement?

D. When payment is due or requested, and whenever the owner demands one — MCL 570.1110 requires the contractor to give the owner a sworn statement when payment is due or requested, and on demand; a sub gives one to the contractor on the same triggers and to the owner on demand.
A contractor records a claim of lien without ever providing the sworn statement the owner requested. What is the status of the lien?

B. Invalid until the sworn statement is provided — Under MCL 570.1110 a contractor or sub that fails to provide a required sworn statement before recording has an invalid lien until it is provided, and a false sworn statement made with intent to defraud is a crime.
An owner receives a sworn statement showing the GC owes a plumbing sub 8,000 dollars. What may the owner do?

A. Rely on it - withhold that amount or pay the sub directly, as a shield against double payment — MCL 570.1110 lets the owner rely on the sworn statement and withhold or pay direct - it is the owner's shield against paying twice for the same work.
After recording a claim of lien, the claimant must serve a copy on whom, and within what time?

C. The designee - or the owner or lessee if none - within 15 days after recording — MCL 570.1111(5) requires service of the recorded claim of lien, personally or by certified mail, on the designee (or owner or lessee if none) within 15 days after recording.
A sub last installed material on May 1, then returned July 15 for a warranty punch-list repair. When does its 90-day recording window run from?

A. May 1 - warranty and punch-list callbacks do not restart the deadline — MCL 570.1111(1) runs the 90-day deadline from the claimant's last furnishing of labor or material, and warranty or punch-list callbacks do not restart it.
On a Michigan public project, the performance bond protects whom?

D. Solely the governmental unit that awarded the contract — MCL 129.201-.202 make the public performance bond protect solely the governmental unit; subs, suppliers, and laborers are protected by the separate payment bond under MCL 129.203.
When a lien claimant files its foreclosure action, what must it also record?
B. A notice of lis pendens — MCL 570.1117(2) requires the claimant to record a notice of lis pendens when filing the foreclosure action.
In a lien foreclosure, when may the court award attorney fees?

C. To a prevailing lien claimant - and to a prevailing defendant if the action was vexatious — MCL 570.1118(2) lets the court award reasonable attorney fees to a prevailing lien claimant, and to a prevailing defendant if the action was vexatious.
A licensed builder does an 80,000 dollar residential addition on a handshake deal with no written contract. Can he lien the home if unpaid?

A. No - a residential lien requires a written contract containing the license number, at any dollar amount — MCL 570.1114 denies a contractor any lien on a residential structure unless the improvement was under a written contract with written change orders containing the statutory licensure statement and license number - with no dollar threshold.
A homeowner discovers a construction lien recorded by an unlicensed contractor. What remedy does the homeowner have?

D. Sue to discharge the lien - the unlicensed recorder is liable for all resulting damages, including actual costs and attorney fees — MCL 570.1114a(2) lets the owner or any affected person sue to discharge a lien recorded by an unlicensed person, who is liable for all damages resulting, including actual costs and attorney fees.
Under Stokes v. Millen Roofing Co., what can an unlicensed residential contractor recover for completed work?

C. Nothing - no contract enforcement, no quantum meruit recovery, and no lien — Stokes v. Millen Roofing Co. (Mich 2002) holds an unlicensed residential contractor cannot enforce the contract, cannot recover in quantum meruit, and has no lien.
A GC's subcontract requires every sub to waive all lien rights before starting work. What is the effect of that clause?

B. Void as contrary to public policy, except to the extent payment was actually made — MCL 570.1115(1) makes an advance lien waiver required as part of the contract, before work is performed, contrary to public policy and invalid except to the extent payment was actually made.
An unpaid sub accepts the GC's promissory note for the balance owed. What happens to the sub's lien rights?
D. Nothing - taking a promissory note does not by itself waive lien rights — MCL 570.1115(1) provides that taking a promissory note does not by itself waive lien rights.
On a residential job, the GC hands the owner a signed lien waiver from an electrical sub. Before relying on it, the owner must:

A. Verify its authenticity with the named claimant - in writing, by telephone, or personally — MCL 570.1115(7) bars a residential owner from relying on a waiver delivered by someone other than the named claimant without verifying its authenticity with the claimant in writing, by phone, or personally.
A sub has received full payment for all of its work. Which lien waiver must it provide?
C. Full unconditional waiver — Under MCL 570.1115 a claimant who has received full payment must provide a full unconditional waiver, effective immediately on signing.
A windstorm destroys a partially framed house along with lumber stored on site. Which coverage responds?

B. Builders risk — Builders risk is first-party property insurance on the structure under construction and materials on site, in transit, or in storage until completion - covering perils like fire, wind, and theft.
A contractor's power tools are stolen from the job site overnight. Does the builders risk policy cover them?

A. No - tools require an inland marine equipment floater — Builders risk covers the structure and installed or stored materials but not tools - tools are covered by an inland-marine equipment floater.
A worker's ladder tips over and dents the neighbor's parked car. Which policy pays for the neighbor's damage?

D. Commercial general liability — CGL is third-party liability coverage for bodily injury and property damage to others arising from the contractor's operations - like a ladder falling on the neighbor's car.
A builder files a CGL claim to pay for tearing out and redoing his own defective tile work. What is the likely result?

B. Denied - the your-work exclusion bars coverage for the insured's own defective work product — CGL does not cover the insured's own work product or defective workmanship - the your-work exclusion; CGL responds to bodily injury and property damage to others.
An employee covered by workers' compensation is injured and wants to sue his employer for negligence. What is the general rule?

C. The suit is generally barred - workers' compensation is the exclusive remedy against the employer — Workers' compensation is statutory no-fault coverage and the exclusive remedy - the employee generally cannot sue the employer in tort (MCL 418.115 framework).
In a contract surety bond, who are the three parties?

A. Principal is the contractor, obligee is the protected owner or government, surety is the bonding company — A surety bond is a three-party guarantee: principal (contractor), obligee (protected owner or government), and surety (bonding company) - and it is not insurance, since the principal must indemnify the surety.
A supplier with no direct contract with the principal contractor is unpaid on a Michigan public project. What notices must it give to claim on the payment bond?

D. Written notice to the principal contractor within 30 days after first furnishing, and notice of the claim to the contractor and governmental unit within 90 days after last furnishing — MCL 129.207 requires a no-privity claimant to serve written notice on the principal contractor within 30 days after first furnishing and give written notice of the claim to the contractor and governmental unit within 90 days after last furnishing, by certified mail.
